component.name: sponux
component.summary: Spotlight-like launcher for Linux: apps, files and a calculator

description.p: sponux is a keyboard launcher for Linux. It searches installed applications, a self-maintained index of filenames under your home directory, and evaluates arithmetic expressions — all in one GTK 4 window opened by a hotkey.

It runs as a single-instance resident daemon: the first call starts it, and every later call toggles the window over D-Bus without starting an interpreter, which is what keeps opening it to about 20 ms.

ul.li: Application search and launch through the desktop's own database, with what you open often floating to the top
Instant filename search, backed by a small SQLite index kept current by inotify; type a path to reach anything it does not cover
A calculator that evaluates expressions without eval(), and copies the result
Places its own window, so no window-manager rules are needed on a tiling or a stacking WM alike
Configurable in config.toml, themeable with a style.css layered over the bundled dark theme

screenshot.caption: Applications and files in one list
Completing a typed path, with no index involved
Arithmetic, evaluated by walking an AST

description.p: Applications are ranked by what you open with them, not only by what you launch by name, and the "open with" list offers your earlier choices first. What the ranking has learned can now be forgotten, with Shift+Delete in the window or --forget from a terminal.
A new application icon, shipped as a vector master alongside the fixed hicolor sizes, so a HiDPI panel no longer scales the 128px one up.

Runtime problems go to a log file instead of a stderr a hotkey-launched process does not have, with desktop notifications for the failures a user can act on. Ships its own icon. A fresh install explains what it is for.
Initial release: application, file and calculator search in a resident GTK 4 daemon toggled over D-Bus.
